odin.dint: Divine intervention in the north: a vast hand of shimmering aurora light reaching down through a raging blizzard to catch a falling, wounded Norse warrior just before he hits the snow, the storm parting around the hand.
odin.karma: Divine Karma, the cosmic tally of deeds in the Norse way: a vast runestone standing in a starry winter sky, every deed of gods and men carved into it as a spiralling serpent band of runes; some runes glow fresh and gold while old.
odin.tdum: A training dummy in a snowy Norse practice yard beside a longhall: a figure of straw and sackcloth tied to a post, wearing a dented iron helmet and an old split wooden shield, axe-cuts all over it.

thoth.dint: Divine intervention: a vast radiant golden hand reaching down from a blazing winged sun disc in the sky to catch a falling, wounded warrior just before he strikes the desert sand.
thoth.karma: Divine Karma in Egypt: the great ledger of the gods, an immense open papyrus book resting on the back of a sacred baboon of Thoth, every deed written in it glowing.
thoth.tblk: A shield dummy: a reed-and-linen training figure on a post holding up a tall cowhide shield in front of itself, standing in a sunlit temple courtyard by the Nile.
thoth.tdum: A training dummy in a temple courtyard by the Nile: a figure of bundled reeds and linen on a wooden post, its face painted with simple eyes, a small wicker shield tied to its arm.

wukong.dint: Divine intervention: a vast radiant golden hand reaching down out of curling auspicious clouds to catch a falling, wounded warrior just before he strikes the mountainside, lotus petals drifting down around it.
wukong.karma: Divine Karma, the cosmic ledger of merit: a giant celestial abacus of glowing jade beads floating among auspicious clouds, the beads sliding by themselves to count good and bad deeds.
wukong.tblk: A shield dummy: a wooden training figure like a wing-chun wooden man, holding a large round rattan shield in front of itself, standing in a bamboo grove practice ground.
wukong.tdum: A training dummy in a temple courtyard on Flower-Fruit Mountain: a straw figure on a wooden post wearing a little red headband, its arms made of bamboo poles, scuffed from staff practice, plum blossom falling.

myth.achil: Achilles in the divine armour Hephaestus made him, leaping forward with his great ash spear, the plain and walls of Troy behind him, his one vulnerable heel just visible.
myth.aegis: Athena's aegis, the goatskin cloak fringed with golden serpents and bearing the Gorgon's head, spread in divine light over a kneeling Greek warrior.
myth.agam: Agamemnon, king of Mycenae and leader of the Greek host at Troy, in gold-trimmed armour, raising his ancestral sceptre to rally the army before the ships.
myth.ajax: Ajax the Great, giant of the Greeks, standing guard before the beached Greek ships behind his huge tower shield of seven ox-hides faced with bronze, calm and immovable, watch-fires glowing in the night behind him.
myth.alcinous: King Alcinous of the Phaeacians on his throne in a palace of bronze walls and golden doors, raising a cup in welcome.
myth.alg: Algiz, the rune of protection: the rune Algiz shining on the face of a round wooden shield, a protective light flaring outward from it.
myth.altar: A stone altar heaped with votive offerings, small clay figurines, garlands and burning fat, glowing in a dark sanctuary.
myth.ammit: Ammit the devourer prowling the Hall of Judgement: the beast with a crocodile's head, a lion's forequarters and a hippo's hindquarters pacing beside the great scales, licking her jaws.
myth.ammt: Devour the unworthy: a heart falling from the pan of the scales into the open jaws of a crocodile-headed beast below.
myth.ansu: Ansuz, the rune of speech: the rune Ansuz glowing in the air in front of an old storyteller's open mouth as he speaks.
myth.anub: The guides of the dead: Anubis, the jackal-headed god, leading a newly dead soul by the hand through the dark of the underworld toward a distant light.
myth.anvl: The anvil of Eitri: a great black iron anvil carved with runes, glowing red-hot with a half-forged ring of gold on it, a hammer resting beside it. The anvil is the whole picture.
myth.apcoil: A chaos coil: the huge coils of a serpent wrapping around a toppled temple column, crushing the stone.
myth.apep: The unmaking: the cat of Ra slicing the head off the serpent Apophis with a knife beneath the sacred persea tree, the serpent's coils thrashing.
myth.apepx: Apophis, the serpent of chaos: an enormous coiling serpent rising out of the dark waters of the underworld to swallow the sun boat of Ra, its mouth wide.
myth.apsp: A spawn of Apophis: a black serpent with red eyes slithering out of a crack in the earth, smoke curling around it.
myth.ares: The great bronze spear of Ares, god of war, standing upright in scorched earth, smoke and embers swirling around it on a ruined battlefield.
myth.argus: Argus, Odysseus's old hound, lying worn and neglected by the palace gate on Ithaca, lifting his head and wagging his tail as he recognises his master, returned after twenty years disguised as a beggar.
myth.augur: A seer like Calchas reading the flight of birds against a stormy sky, arms raised, the Greek fleet waiting below.
myth.bald: Baldr the Beautiful, the shining god whom nothing could harm: a young, serene god with pale gold hair, a calm face and a faint cold light about him, in a white wool tunic with a gold-trimmed cloak.
myth.banner: A war standard on a tall pole, a crimson banner snapping in the wind over the Greek camp at Troy, the beached black ships behind.
myth.bastion: Spartan warriors in red cloaks standing shoulder to shoulder as a living wall before unwalled Sparta, because its men were its walls, Mount Taygetus behind.
myth.bcap: A buffalo captain: a water-buffalo demon officer with curved horns and a heavy halberd, riding a war cart.
myth.bdk: The Bull Demon King, sworn brother turned enemy of the Monkey King: a colossal demon king with a black bull's head and huge horns, in black and gold armour, gripping a mixed-iron cudgel, his eyes burning red.
myth.bdrunk: A blood-drunk berserker: a wild-eyed warrior laughing in the snow with his own blood running down his bare, rune-painted arms, swaying as if drunk, an axe in each hand, steam rising off him in the cold.
myth.bfury: The fury of the bull: a vast white bull of smoke and fire rearing over a burning mountain, its horns scraping the clouds.
myth.bghl: A wandering corpse: a pale hopping corpse in a Qing official's robe and hat with a yellow talisman on its forehead, hopping through a moonlit bamboo forest.
myth.bgrd: A bull guard: a hulking bull-headed demon in iron armour with a huge iron club, nostrils steaming.
myth.bhag: The old hag: the White Bone Spirit disguised as a frail old woman with a walking stick on a mountain path, her shadow on the ground a skeleton.
myth.bhrn: A horned vanguard: a bull demon charging head-down with its great horns lowered, dust exploding behind it.
myth.blackship: The swift black ship of the Phaeacians gliding home over a moonlit sea, the moment before Poseidon turns it to stone.
myth.bland: Scorched earth: a burnt Norse farmstead, charred longhouse frames and blackened fields smoking under a red sky, embers drifting.
myth.bldr: A blood rite: a bowl of blood held up over a stone altar by a priest's hands, the blood splashed across a carved runestone and running into the snow.
myth.blod: A blood-drinker berserker: a gaunt warrior with blood smeared across his mouth and chest, drinking from a horn of blood before battle, wild eyes, a bearskin over his shoulders.
myth.blot: A blót bowl: a heavy bronze sacrificial bowl full of dark blood standing on a stone altar, a bundle of fir twigs lying in it for sprinkling the blood, carved knotwork on its rim, firelight from a temple hall behind.
myth.bodvar: Bodvar Bjarki, the bear-spirit hero of Hrolf Kraki's saga: a huge, calm warrior sitting as if asleep while the great spirit of a red-brown bear rises from his body behind him, the bear towering and roaring.
myth.bone: The corpse-shedding form: an empty discarded human body lying on a mountain path while a ghostly white skeleton figure drifts away from it in the mist.
myth.bow: The great bow of Odysseus that none of the suitors could string, drawn at last in his hall, an arrow flying through the line of twelve axe-heads.
myth.bragi: Bragi, god of poetry: a long-bearded god with runes tattooed on his tongue, singing with a golden harp, the words of his song turning into glowing runes that drift around him in the air.
myth.brasidas: Brasidas, the bold Spartan general, leading his men on a night march through the mountains of Thrace, red cloak and crested helmet in moonlight.
myth.breeze: A warm, gentle island breeze sweeping through palms and lotus flowers on a sunlit shore, petals drifting in the air.
myth.brokk: Brokkr, the master smith who forged Mjolnir: an old dwarf with a huge white beard pumping a great bellows with all his might while a fly stings his eyelid, the forge blazing.
myth.brute: A hulking one-eyed Cyclops warrior with a great wooden club, glaring, standing on rocky ground.
myth.brynh: Brynhild the valkyrie from the Volsunga saga, who defied Odin and was cast into an enchanted sleep inside a ring of fire on the mountain Hindarfjall: she stands awake at the heart of the wall of flame in a long iron mail byrnie an.
myth.bsk: A bone soldier: a skeleton warrior in rusted lamellar armour with a broken halberd, rising out of a misty graveyard.
myth.bsp: The White Bone Spirit in her true form: a beautiful pale woman in white robes whose body is half a skeleton, bone fingers reaching out, mist curling around her.
myth.bsrk: A Bear-Shirt berserker in the grip of battle-fury: a huge bearded warrior wearing a bear's head and pelt as a cloak, biting the rim of his round wooden shield, eyes rolled wild, an axe raised; snow and sparks around him.
myth.bull: A massive sacred bull of Helios with a sun disc glowing between its horns, standing guard over the herd on Thrinacia.
myth.burn: Granaries burning in the night at Ismarus, sparks rising over the fields.
myth.camp: A ragged camp follower in the Greek camp on the beach at Troy, carrying a basket and a water jar between the beached black ships and smoking cook-fires.
myth.canto: The Song of the Sirens made visible as golden ribbons of light flowing over the sea toward Odysseus's ship.
myth.capt: A veteran hoplite captain in a tall horsehair-crested helmet pointing his sword forward, ordering his shield line to advance.
myth.cass: Cassandra, the cursed prophetess of Troy, wild-haired and crying out her warning that no one believes, as the great wooden horse is dragged through the gates behind her.
myth.cave: A shaggy cave beast with glowing eyes lurking in the dark mouth of a cave on the island of the Cyclopes, old bones on the ground.
myth.cbow: A Cicone slinger whirling a leather sling above his head on a rocky hillside.
myth.cdraft: Circe's cup of drugged wine mixed with cheese, barley and honey, a faint green glow rising from it.
myth.cdro: A drowned sailor's pale ghost rising from the dark sea, seaweed in his hair, eyes empty and sad.
myth.ceel: A great eel coiling through the churning waters near Charybdis, sleek and fast.
myth.censer: A bronze censer hanging from chains, pouring out thick, sweet-smelling poppy smoke in a dim island shrine.
myth.cerb: Cerberus, the colossal three-headed hound of Hades, with a serpent for a tail and snakes along his back, snarling with glowing ember eyes at the gates of the underworld, the river Styx and green-black mist behind.
myth.charon: Charon, the grim old ferryman of the dead, poling his boat across the dark river Styx, pale shades waiting on the bank, a coin for the fare in his outstretched hand.
myth.chary: Charybdis, the devouring whirlpool beneath the fig tree on the cliff, sucking down the dark sea into a vast spiral.
myth.chief: The chieftain of Ismarus, a fierce Thracian lord in a fur cloak and bronze helmet, holding a war banner on a hill.
myth.circe: Circe, daughter of Helios, the enchantress of Aeaea, singing at her great loom in her stone hall, a golden wand at her side.
myth.clev: A huge leviathan breaching from the dark sea near the whirlpool, its back like a reef.
myth.clion: A mountain lion of Aeaea, tame and strangely gentle under Circe's spell, prowling in the forest around her palace.
myth.closer: Close ranks: a line of Greek hoplites slamming their round shields together into an overlapping wall at the shout of their officer, spears levelled over the rims, dust rising around their feet.
myth.club: The great olive-wood club of the Cyclops lying in his cave, as long as a ship's mast, beside a dying fire.
myth.cmaid: One of Circe's handmaids, a nymph of the springs and groves, carrying a silver bowl of healing herbs.
myth.cocn: A cocoon: a warrior wrapped head to toe in glowing white spider silk, hanging upside down from a cave ceiling, only his angry eyes visible.
myth.corp: Corpse-cold: the grey, frozen realm of Hel, a field of frost-covered dead warriors standing silent in the mist, all facing the same way.
myth.corsair: A Cicone raider from Thrace leaping from a small boat onto a beach, blade raised, painted shield on his arm.
myth.cow: A sacred cow of Helios, broad-browed with gilded horns, grazing in a golden meadow on the island of Thrinacia.
myth.croc: A Nile crocodile: a huge crocodile bursting out of the river shallows with its jaws wide open, water and spray flying.
myth.cscout: A one-eyed Cyclops herder with a heavy stone hammer, standing on a hillside above his flocks on the island of the Cyclopes.
myth.cspa: A small creature of swirling sea foam and spray, shaped like a crouching otter-like beast, rising from a churning patch of dark green sea near a rocky strait.
myth.cup: Circe's golden cup on a stone table in her palace, enchanted drink shimmering inside, pigs in the shadows behind.
myth.curse: A withering curse: a dark, sickly mist curling around a bronze shield and helmet, tarnishing them as it spreads.
myth.curse2: The curse of the pharaoh: a tomb robber recoiling in terror as a sealed tomb door bursts open, a cold wind and glowing eyes rushing out of the dark.
myth.cwand: Circe's golden wand glowing with enchantment, a faint swirl of light and a startled pig at her feet.
myth.cweb: The cobweb: a vast web of shining silk filling the whole mouth of Silk Cave, catching the moonlight like a net of silver, shapes of trapped travellers in it.
myth.cwolf: A great grey mountain wolf, enchanted by Circe, fawning gently with its tail wagging outside her stone palace on Aeaea.
myth.dakh: Akh, the glorified: a reunited soul shining with light like a star, a figure of radiant gold rising from a tomb into the sky, the Ka and Ba merging into it.
myth.dammit: The devouring jaws: Ammit, the devourer of the dead, part crocodile, part lion and part hippopotamus, lunging forward with her crocodile jaws wide open to swallow a heart that has failed the judgement.
myth.dbal: A soul-bird keeper: an old priest gently holding a Ba-bird, a small falcon with a human head, on his wrist in a tomb chapel lit by lamps.
myth.dbolt: A dwarven bolt: a heavy iron crossbow bolt with rune-cut fins, glowing hot, flying out of the dark toward the viewer.
myth.dbook: The Book of Gates: a long painted papyrus unrolled across a tomb floor, showing the night journey of the sun boat through the twelve gates of the underworld, glowing serpents guarding each gate.
myth.dbrth: Dragon's breath: a torrent of fire and poison pouring from an unseen dragon's jaws across a rocky slope, scorching everything in its path.
myth.dcart: A cartouche ring: a gold ring shaped as a royal cartouche, an oval with a loop of rope, set with carnelian and turquoise, resting on a cushion. The ring is the whole picture.
myth.dcut: A ritual knife: a curved flint ritual knife with a gold handle lying on an alabaster offering table beside lotus flowers and a bowl. The knife is the whole picture.
myth.dduat: The gate of the Duat: one of the twelve fiery gates of the underworld, a tall pylon guarded by a great serpent coiled along the top and fire-breathing cobras at its doors, the boat of the sun waiting in the dark river before it.
myth.decree: A heavenly decree: a long yellow imperial scroll unrolling through the clouds, stamped with the red seal of the Jade Emperor, glowing calligraphy on it.
myth.dembal: An embalmer: a priest in a jackal mask of Anubis bending over a body wrapped in linen on a lion-shaped embalming table, holding a jar of resin and a strip of linen, canopic jars lined up beside him.
myth.dheart: A heart scarab: a large green stone scarab carved with a spell on its underside, set into a gold frame on the chest of a mummy, glowing faintly.
myth.dint: Divine intervention: a vast shining hand reaching down through parting storm clouds to catch a falling, wounded warrior just before he strikes the ground, pure golden light pouring through the gap in the clouds.
myth.dio2: Diomedes the Bold driving his spear at the war god Ares himself with Athena's help, fire blazing from his helmet as the Iliad describes.
myth.dirge: A sorrowful dirge of the deep: Sirens singing on a cliff under a pale moon, a lone bronze bell on a rock, a ghost-grey sea.
myth.dkhep: Khepri's rebirth: the scarab god Khepri, a great golden scarab beetle, rolling the newborn red sun up over the eastern horizon at dawn.
myth.dmin: A dwarf miner: a short, broad dwarf with a braided beard and a leather cap, swinging a pick at a glowing seam of gold in a dark tunnel, lantern on his belt.
myth.dmum: A mummy of the Old Kingdom: an ancient royal mummy in faded linen and a cracked gold mask, rising from its stone sarcophagus in a dusty tomb, its painted eyes glowing.
myth.dnomad: A wandering Ba: a little human-headed bird soul flying out of a tomb shaft into the evening sky over the desert, looking back at the tomb.
myth.doct: A disciplined phalanx seen head-on: rows of round bronze shields locked rim to rim, spears held upright, crested helmets, dust rising around them.
myth.dosir: Osiris, lord of the dead: the green-skinned king of the underworld seated on his throne, wrapped in white linen like a mummy, wearing the tall white atef crown with two ostrich plumes.
myth.dpart: The parting of souls: a pale ghostly double stepping out of a sleeping man's body in a dim tomb, a small human-headed bird hovering above them.
myth.drag: Drag below: a hand reaching out of a dark tomb shaft to grab a guard's ankle and pull him down into the blackness.
myth.draug: A draugr, a restless corpse risen from its grave mound: a bloated, blue-black dead warrior in rotted mail with pale glowing eyes, climbing out of a barrow at night.
myth.dream: Odysseus's sailors asleep in the long grass of the lotus island, smiling in their dreams, as dreamy mist drifts over them at dusk.
myth.dren: Names of the dead: rows of carved royal cartouches on a dark tomb wall glowing gold one by one as a priest's lamp passes over them.
myth.dreun: Reunion in the Field of Reeds: a man and his Ba-bird reunited in the paradise of the Field of Reeds, ploughing golden wheat beside blue canals under a perfect sky.
myth.drill: Greek soldiers drilling in formation on a dusty training ground beneath a mountain, a scarred old instructor shouting the time.
myth.drpn: Draupnir, the ring of gold: a thick gold arm-ring with eight smaller rings dripping from it like drops, resting on black velvet-dark stone, glowing softly.
myth.drums: Thracian war drums of hide and wood beaten at dawn on a hillside, warriors gathering in the mist behind.
myth.dsever: Sever the mighty: a giant enemy warrior's great shadow being cut away from his body by a priest's knife of light, the warrior staggering.
myth.dshade: Sheut, the shadow: a long black shadow-soul stretching across a sunlit temple floor, standing up on its own and walking away from the body that cast it.
myth.dshld: A dwarf-forged shield: a round shield of dark iron and gold inlay with an interlaced dragon pattern, hanging on the stone wall of a forge, firelight on its boss.
myth.dsk: A Ka-keeper: a priestess tending a row of painted Ka statues in a tomb's statue chamber, offering bread and beer, each statue with the raised-arms Ka sign on its head.
myth.dsmith: A dwarf smith: a stocky dwarf with a singed beard and leather apron, lifting a red-hot blade from the forge with tongs, sparks around him.
myth.dsoul: A soul-collector: a gaunt priest in a black panther skin walking through a desert necropolis at dusk with a net full of fluttering human-headed Ba-birds.
myth.dsplit: The scattering of the pieces: fragments of a broken statue of a king flying apart in a burst of dust and light, its pieces scattering across the desert.
myth.dtwof: The amulet of the two feathers: a gold amulet of two tall plumes standing side by side, set with lapis and turquoise inlay, catching the desert light.
myth.dweigh: A weigher of souls: an assessor of the dead, a stern god with a feather on his head sitting in judgement, holding up a small set of golden scales.
myth.dwrap: Linen wrappings: long strips of fine white linen unrolling through the air around a mummy shape, amulets tucked between the layers glinting.
myth.dxbow: A dwarf crossbowman: a helmeted dwarf in heavy mail kneeling behind a rock and aiming a heavy iron crossbow straight at the viewer.
myth.eagle: The great golden eagle of Zeus with a thunderbolt clutched in its talons, wings spread wide against storm clouds.
myth.eel: A huge moray eel lunging from a dark rocky crevice below the Sirens' island, jaws open, in green-blue water.
myth.eerl: Erlang Shen, the Illustrious Sage: a handsome, stern god with a third eye blazing on his forehead, in silver armour and a yellow cloak, holding his three-pointed double-edged blade.
myth.egil: Egil the Mad, the poet-warrior of Egil's saga: a huge, ugly, heavy-browed man with a wild beard, laughing as he chants a verse with an axe in his fist, drinking horn in the other hand, firelit.
myth.ehnd: The howling celestial hound: Erlang Shen's loyal black hunting dog, lean and fierce, leaping with jaws open across a rocky mountain.
myth.ein: An einherjar newly risen: a slain warrior stepping out of a shaft of golden light from Valhalla's roof of shields, his wounds closing, sword in hand, his face calm and proud.
myth.einw: An einherjar warrior, one of the slain heroes of Valhalla: a warrior with healed battle wounds and a calm, proud face, in mail and a gold-trimmed cloak, holding a sword, light from the shields that roof Valhalla falling on him.
myth.eir: Eir the healer, goddess of healing: a calm woman in a pale green cloak kneeling beside a wounded warrior, holding a bowl of herbs and a cup, her hands glowing faintly.
myth.elder: An ancient grey-bearded Cyclops elder with his single wise, weary eye, leaning on a gnarled staff outside his cave.
myth.ember: An ember sprite: a small, flickering fire spirit shaped like a laughing imp made of embers and sparks, darting over glowing coals.
myth.embp: An embalming priest: an old priest with a jar of natron salt and a bundle of linen in the House of Purification, preparing a body on a stone table.
myth.eplum: A Plum Mountain brother: one of Erlang Shen's six sworn brothers, a bearded hunter-warrior in green with a bow and a falcon on his arm, among plum blossom.
myth.esw: The three-pointed blade: Erlang Shen's long-hafted trident-sword with three double-edged points, flashing as it sweeps through the air. The weapon is the whole picture.
myth.eury: Eurylochus, Odysseus's kinsman and second-in-command, a hard bearded sailor-warrior leading the crew ashore on Circe's island with a drawn sword, wary of the forest.
myth.eye: The third eye: a single vertical eye opening on a god's forehead in extreme close-up, beams of white light shining out and revealing hidden shapes.
myth.fafn: Fafnir the hoard-dragon: a huge serpentine dragon coiled on a mountain of gold rings and treasure, its scales glinting gold, its eyes greedy and burning.
myth.fate: The well of Urd: a deep, still well beneath the vast roots of the world-tree, its water glowing silver-white, swans gliding on its surface.
myth.fbolt: A searing bolt: a lance of white-hot fire streaking from a dark sky toward the ground, scorching the snow into steam.
myth.fehu: Fehu, the rune of wealth: the rune Fehu carved into a gold arm-ring on top of a heap of silver hacksilver and coins in a wooden chest.
myth.fence: A black-market fence: a sly merchant in a dim market stall weighing stolen gold amulets on a small balance, a curtain half hiding crates of grave goods.
myth.fenr: Fenrir unbound: the monstrous wolf, as big as a hall, his jaws opened so wide they touch earth and sky, the broken silken fetter Gleipnir hanging from his neck, eyes burning, the world shaking around him.
myth.ffire: The forge-fire: the great forge of the dwarves blazing inside a mountain hall, molten gold pouring from a crucible into a mould, the whole cavern lit gold and red.
myth.fgrd: A hoard-guard: a grim armoured warrior standing guard in a treasure cave, gold to his knees, his eyes gone gold with greed.
myth.fjrd: A fjord raider leaping from the prow of a longship onto a rocky shore: a young Norse raider in leather and fur with an axe and a round shield, the carved dragon prow rising behind him, spray flying.
myth.fog: A creeping narcotic fog rolling over the beached black ships of Odysseus, sailors slumped drowsily on the oars.
myth.fraid: A flame raider of Muspelheim: a warrior with skin like cracked charcoal glowing with lava beneath, a burning sword in his hand, flames for hair.
myth.freyja: Freyja, lady of the slain, who takes half of those who die in battle to her hall Folkvangr: a beautiful, fierce goddess with golden hair, wearing the shining necklace Brisingamen and a cloak of falcon feathers.
myth.fspit: Venom spit: a glob of green venom flying from a dragon's mouth, hissing as it spatters on a shield and melts the wood.
myth.fury: Ares, god of war, in a crested helmet and wreathed in red fire, gripping a mortal warrior's arm and filling him with sudden battle-rage.
myth.fworm: A lindworm: a long, limbless wingless dragon-serpent with two clawed forelegs, slithering through a dark marsh, its jaws open.
myth.fylg: A fylgja, a guardian spirit: a translucent white she-wolf of light walking beside a sleeping warrior in the snow, watching over him.
myth.gald: Galdr of winds: a rune-singer on a cliff edge chanting with her arms out, the wind she calls tearing at her cloak and hair and whipping the sea below.
myth.gale: The bag of winds of Aeolus torn open by Odysseus's crew: a howling gale bursts from the leather sack and hurls the ship back across the wine-dark sea, away from the shores of Ithaca.
myth.games: The funeral games for Patroclus at Troy: chariots racing around a turning post, the burial mound behind, crowds of warriors cheering.
myth.garden: The lush Lotus Garden of the Lotus-Eaters, pale lotus flowers and fruit trees under golden afternoon haze.
myth.gash: A spear-gash: a warrior pressing his hand to a fresh wound on his side, blood between his fingers, gritting his teeth with fierce resolve, spear still in his other hand.
myth.gate: A guard standing before the Lion Gate of Mycenae, two carved lionesses above the massive stone lintel, his spear barring the way, torchlight on the stone.
myth.gcanop: Canopic jars: the four canopic jars of alabaster with lids shaped as the heads of a man, a baboon, a jackal and a falcon, standing in a row in a painted chest.
myth.gfeather: The feather of Ma'at: a single tall white ostrich feather standing upright on a gold base, radiating calm light. The feather is the whole picture.
myth.ghall: The hall of the slain: the great hall of Valhalla, its roof made of golden shields and its rafters of spears, long tables of feasting warriors, seen down its full length.
myth.gift: A table of gifts of hospitality: a golden cup, a fine cloak, a tripod and bread and wine, set out for a guest in a Greek hall.
myth.gnile: The gift of the Nile: the river in flood, green fields and palm trees on its banks, a fisherman's papyrus boat and a crocodile in the shallows, the god Hapi pouring water from jars.
myth.golem: An iron golem forged by the dwarves: a hulking figure of riveted black iron plates and glowing rune seams, steam venting from its joints, its fists like anvils.
myth.gourd: The gourd of names: a red lacquered gourd hanging on a cord, glowing, with names in gold calligraphy swirling into its mouth like smoke.
myth.gpriest: A priest of Thoth: a shaven-headed priest in white linen with a panther skin over one shoulder, carrying a small statue of an ibis in procession.
myth.grob: A grave robber: a wiry thief in a dusty loincloth and headcloth prising the gold mask off a mummy by the light of a single oil lamp, glancing nervously over his shoulder.
myth.gscroll: A scroll of protection: a small papyrus scroll of spells rolled and tied with red thread, glowing as it shields a sleeping child from shadowy demons at the edge of the room.
myth.gslay: A giant-slayer standing triumphant on the chest of a fallen frost giant whose huge body stretches across the picture like a snowy hill, his axe raised high over his head, ice crystals in the giant's enormous beard.
myth.gung: Gungnir's throw: the spear Gungnir, its head carved with runes, flying straight at the viewer through the air, trailing cold light, the hand that threw it only a shadow far behind. The spear is the whole picture.
myth.gunn: Gunnar, the hall-warden: a strong, gallant warrior at the gates of a hall, sword drawn and shield up, his long hair tied back, ready to hold the doorway alone.
myth.gweigh: The weighing of the heart: the great golden scales of judgement in the Hall of Two Truths, a human heart on one pan and the white feather of Ma'at on the other.
myth.hades: Hades, Lord of the Dead, enthroned in the dark underworld with a dark crown and two-pronged staff, Cerberus at his feet, pale shades drifting in the distance.
myth.hagl: Hagalaz, the rune of hail: a storm of huge hailstones falling from a black sky onto a battlefield, the rune Hagalaz flashing in the clouds.
myth.hammer: Hephaestus, the lame smith god, at his forge inside a volcano, hammer raised over the anvil, sparks and molten light flying.
myth.hamr: Hamramr the shape-shifter, mid-transformation: a warrior whose head has become a snarling brown bear's head with a muzzle and fangs while his body is still a man in torn mail and a cloak.
myth.harrier: A raider blowing a horn from the prow of a ship as a pack of boats rushes into a harbour town at dawn.
myth.hati: Hati, the wolf who chases the moon: an enormous pale silver wolf leaping across the night sky toward a huge full moon, its jaws open, stars caught in its fur.
myth.hbot: The jade-purity bottle: a small white jade vase with a gold stopper, its mouth sucking in a whirlwind of light and a tiny shrinking figure.
myth.hcap: A cave captain: a stout horned demon officer in patched leather armour, barking orders with a whip in his hand, a red banner behind him.
myth.hchar: A Trojan charioteer driving two horses at full gallop across the plain of Troy.
myth.hdead: The hungry dead of Hades crowding around a trench of dark offerings, pale and longing, in the grey twilight of Erebus.
myth.heads: Scylla's six heads seen from the deck of a ship, rising from the cliff cave into the mist, each on its long neck.
myth.heal2: The waters of the Nile: a priest pouring water from a tall silver jar over a wounded warrior on the riverbank, the water glowing with healing light.
myth.hearth: The great hearth of Odysseus's hall on Ithaca, the fire burning low; in the shadows Penelope's loom holds the burial shroud she weaves by day and unravels by night.
myth.hecat: A hecatomb, the great sacrifice of a hundred oxen: altar fires burning in a row along the seashore, thick smoke rising to the gods.
myth.hector: Hector, Tamer of Horses and prince of Troy, in gleaming armour with a tall horse-hair crest, standing before the walls of Troy.
myth.heka: Execration: a priest smashing red clay pots inscribed with the names of enemies, the shards flying and dark smoke rising from them.
myth.hekhigh: The high priest of Heka: an imposing high priest in a leopard skin and gold collar raising an ivory magic wand carved with protective creatures, light swirling around it.
myth.hekmag: A magician of the court: a court magician performing before the pharaoh, turning his staff into a living serpent on the palace floor.
myth.hekp: A priest of Heka: a priest with a shaven head holding a pair of serpent-shaped magic wands, speaking a spell over a sick child.
myth.hela: Hel's embrace: the goddess Hel, half of her face pale and beautiful and half dark and dead, reaching out her arms in a cold, gloomy underworld.
myth.helios: Helios the sun god, crowned with rays of light, driving his blazing four-horse chariot across the sky.
myth.herm: Hermes, messenger of the gods, in his winged sandals and winged cap with his herald's staff, flying swiftly over the sea with a message from Olympus.
myth.hgn: A heavenly general: a fierce celestial general with a painted red face, a long black beard and gold armour with tiger-head shoulders, pointing his sword forward from a cloud chariot.
myth.hgnt: A hill giant: a huge, craggy giant with skin like grey stone and moss in his beard, rising from a mountainside with a tree trunk for a club, tiny pines at his knees.
myth.hgod: The hanged god: Odin hanging from a branch of the world-tree Yggdrasil for nine nights, wounded by his own spear, gaunt and pale.
myth.hgol: The Gold Horn King: a heavy demon king with a single golden horn and golden skin, in gold brocade armour, holding the magic gourd and a seven-star sword.
myth.hgrasp: The grasp of the grave: pale dead hands bursting up through cold earth and snow to seize a warrior's ankles.
myth.hgrd: A Hel-guard: a tall armoured guardian of Hel's gate, half its body fleshless bone, holding a long spear before the black gate of the underworld.
myth.hgrt: A gravel giant: a huge giant whose whole body is built of stacked boulders and loose gravel, clearly a giant with a head, arms and legs, striding down a mountain slope with stones and dust pouring off him at every step.
myth.hgua: An elite Ilian guard in heavy bronze armour with a tall rectangular shield, holding the gate of Troy.
myth.hguard: A hall-guard of Valhalla: a giant warrior in gold-trimmed mail standing at one of Valhalla's five hundred and forty doors, a spear crossed in front of the door.
myth.hguard2: The guardian of the scales: a huge baboon of Thoth seated on top of the beam of the great scales of judgement, watching the balance.
myth.hhbt: A hunter's spear: a long ghostly spear flying through a stormy night sky, trailing pale light.
myth.hhd: A celestial hound: a sleek white dog of heaven with a golden collar and flame-like fur, leaping across the clouds, teeth bared.
myth.hhnd: A Hel-hound of the Wild Hunt: a black ghost-hound with burning eyes and smoke streaming from its fur, running through a stormy night sky.
myth.hhrn: The horn of the hunt: a great carved hunting horn blown in the storm, its sound shown as rings of ghostly light spreading across the sky.
myth.hird: A hirdman, a sworn warrior of a Norse lord's household: a sturdy bearded man in a mail shirt and a plain iron helmet with a nose guard, a round painted wooden shield on his arm and a spear held ready.
myth.hitr: Cicone horsemen wheeling away into the hills at dawn after striking the Greek camp, dust trailing behind them.
myth.hmead: Giant's mead: an enormous drinking horn overflowing with mead, held in a giant's stone hand.
myth.hmil: A Trojan militiaman, an ordinary townsman with a simple shield and spear, standing on the walls of Troy.
myth.hmokk: Mokkurkalfi, the clay giant built by the giants to fight Thor: a huge, lumpy, red-brown giant of wet clay standing knee-deep in a muddy plain, rain streaming down him.
myth.hmst: The huntmaster of the Gandreid: a grim, one-eyed leader of the Wild Hunt in a wide hat, riding a great horse at the head of a ghostly host through the night sky.
myth.hnet: The heaven-and-earth net: a vast golden net cast across the sky by heavenly soldiers, falling over a mountain and its forests.
myth.hnz: Nezha, the third prince, in his battle form with three heads and six arms, each arm holding a weapon, the red Armillary Sash whirling around him, standing on fire wheels in the clouds.
myth.hoard: The hoard of Andvari: a heap of gold rings, cups and coins glittering in a cave, with the cursed ring Andvaranaut at the top shining brightest.
myth.hoff: The hanged man's offering: a gallows tree on a windswept hill at dusk with a noose hanging empty, gold rings, a spear and a sacrificed rooster laid at its roots as gifts to Odin.
myth.holm: The holmgang: two warriors facing each other in a duel inside a square marked by hazel stakes and a cloak spread on the ground, shields up.
myth.honey: A honeyed offering of cakes and a golden bowl of honey left on a sea rock to calm the waters.
myth.hopl: An Argive warrior behind a towering Mycenaean figure-of-eight body shield, wearing a boar's-tusk helmet as Homer describes, braced and immovable on the plain of Troy.
myth.horde: A mounted charge of Amazon warriors across a plain, axes and spears raised, horses at full gallop in a storm of dust.
myth.horse: The Trojan Horse: the colossal wooden horse standing before the great walls of Troy at dawn, built from the timbers of the Greek ships and taller than the gate, a small hatch in its belly barely visible.
myth.host: The host of Valhalla: a line of ghostly einherjar warriors riding out of a cloud bank on horseback, shields and spears catching the light, led by a valkyrie.
myth.howl: A war howl before battle: a wolf-coated warrior with his head thrown back and mouth wide open, howling up at a huge full moon, the wolf skull of his pelt over his brow, breath steaming in the cold.
myth.hpg: The pagoda-bearing heavenly king Li Jing: a stern armoured king holding up a small glowing golden pagoda in one palm, its light pinning the ground below.
myth.hrav: Hrafnagud, the raven-god: Odin as a great shadowy raven-shape with outstretched wings and one glowing eye, its feathers turning into a dark cloak.
myth.hrdr: A phantom rider: a pale, translucent rider on a skeletal horse, galloping through the clouds with a spear, his cloak torn by the wind.
myth.hrope: The humbling rope: a golden magic rope coiling through the air on its own like a snake, tying itself around a struggling warrior's arms.
myth.hrung: Hrungnir, the stone-hearted, strongest of the giants: a colossal giant with a head and heart of stone, carrying a great stone shield and a whetstone club, standing on a barren mountain.
myth.hsd: A heavenly soldier: a celestial infantryman in shining gilded scale armour and a plumed helmet, standing in formation on a cloud with a halberd.
myth.hsil: The Silver Horn King: a slender demon king with a single silver horn and pale silver skin, in silver robes, raising the magic Jade-Purity bottle with a sly smile.
myth.hsol: A horn soldier: a scruffy demon soldier with small horns and a crooked spear, standing guard at the door of Lotus Flower Cave, yawning.
myth.hspr: A Trojan spearman in a crested helmet before the Scaean Gates of Troy, spear ready.
myth.htrl: A rock-troll: a hunched troll with skin like lichen-covered stone, long arms and a tusked jaw, lurking at the mouth of a cave.
myth.hugi: Huginn, Odin's raven of Thought: a black raven in flight whose spread wings and trailing feathers dissolve into glowing threads, flowing runes and branching lines of light like the paths of a thinking mind, a faint.
myth.hunt: The Wild Hunt: a host of ghostly riders and hounds sweeping across a stormy winter night sky above a small frightened village.
myth.hurl: Blinded Polyphemus hurling a huge boulder from the cliffs toward Odysseus's escaping ship, a great splash in the sea.
myth.huscl: A housecarl, a lord's bodyguard: a huge warrior with a long Dane-axe and a kite shield, standing in front of his lord with his feet planted, unmovable.
myth.hwhet: The whetstone of Hrungnir: a huge jagged whetstone hurled through the air, shattering as it meets a lightning bolt.
myth.hwld: A wild huntsman: a cloaked rider with a hunting horn at his lips, mounted on a black horse, leaping across the storm clouds.
myth.ianx: The ankh of life: a large golden ankh glowing with life, held out by a god's hand toward the lips of a kneeling pharaoh. The ankh is the focus.
myth.icesp: An ice spear: a long jagged spear of blue ice flying through a snowstorm, frost trailing behind it. The spear is the whole picture.
myth.ichisel: A chisel: a sculptor's copper chisel and wooden mallet chipping a name out of a carved stone relief, chips of stone flying.
myth.idjed: The djed pillar: a tall pillar of stacked bands, the backbone of Osiris, raised upright by priests with ropes in a temple ceremony.
myth.idun: Idunn's apples, the apples of youth that keep the gods young: three ripe golden apples, clearly apples with stems and leaves, resting in a simple carved ash-wood bowl lined with moss.
myth.ierase: Damnatio, the erasure: a wall relief of a pharaoh whose face and name have been chiselled away, the stone fresh and raw where the image used to be.
myth.ieye: The Eye of Horus, the wedjat: a huge golden-and-lapis wedjat-eye amulet floating in the air, its painted eye opening and looking out, rays of light spreading from it. The eye is the whole picture.
myth.ifan: The banana-leaf fan: the magical palm-leaf fan alone, as tall as a man, standing upright in a stone hall, its veins glowing faintly. The fan is the whole picture.
myth.iglyph: A glyph-warded guard: a temple guard in a white kilt with a tall spear and shield, protective symbols painted in red on his chest and arms glowing faintly.
myth.iguard: A palm-leaf guard: a stocky guard with a huge round shield shaped like a palm leaf, standing at the gate of Palm-Leaf Cave.
myth.ihekau: Words of heka, words of power: a magician-priest with arms raised speaking a spell, golden glyph-shapes of power streaming from his mouth and swirling around a war chariot.
myth.iink: The ink of Seshat: a scribe's palette with cakes of red and black ink, a reed pen dipping in, the ink rising from the palette in a glowing curl.
myth.ikhem: The keeper of sacred texts: an old priest in a leopard skin standing before tall niches stacked with papyrus rolls in the House of Life, a single lamp in his hand.
myth.iliv: A living papyrus: a long papyrus scroll that has come alive, rising and twisting like a serpent, its painted figures stepping out of its surface.
myth.imaid: A fan maiden: a servant of Princess Iron Fan in green silk, carrying a large palm-leaf fan on her shoulder through the Palm-Leaf Cave.
myth.imp: A sly imp: a small, grinning trickster spirit with pointed ears and long fingers, perched on a drinking horn and pouring mead into a sleeping warrior's ear.
myth.iname: The unspoken name: an empty golden cartouche, an oval ring of rope with nothing written inside, glowing alone in total darkness in a sealed tomb chamber, a single shaft of light falling on it. No person and no god.
myth.inarm: The palette of Narmer: the great carved stone ceremonial palette of the first king, standing in a pool of light, its relief showing the king striking his enemy.
myth.iobel: The obelisk of words: a towering red granite obelisk with a gold-capped top catching the first sun, standing before a temple pylon, tiny people at its base for scale.
myth.iph: Iphigenia, daughter of Agamemnon, standing calmly at the altar at Aulis in a white robe as the goddess Artemis spirits her away and a deer appears in her place in a burst of light, the becalmed fleet behind.
myth.iprin: Princess Iron Fan, the rakshasa wife of the Bull Demon King, at home in Palm-Leaf Cave: seated on a carved throne in red and gold robes, her giant palm-leaf fan resting across her lap, eyes narrowed and suspicious.
myth.iris: Iris, goddess of the rainbow and swift messenger of the gods, with golden wings, descending along a rainbow through storm clouds.
myth.isac: Sacred text: a priest reading aloud from a long papyrus scroll in a dark sanctuary, the words he speaks rising from the page as a stream of golden light.
myth.iscribe: An apprentice scribe: a boy with the sidelock of youth practising hieroglyphs on a limestone flake, tongue between his teeth in concentration, an older scribe watching.
myth.iseshat: Seshat, mistress of books and goddess of writing: a woman in a leopard-skin robe with a seven-pointed star crowned by a bow on her head, writing on a long palm rib with a reed pen, measuring cords coiled at her side.
myth.ishen: The shen ring: a gold shen ring, a circle of rope with a straight bar at the bottom, held in the talons of a falcon with outspread wings.
myth.isl: A dazed islander of the Lotus-Eaters lying content in tall grass by the shore, a half-eaten lotus fruit in his hand, eyes heavy and dreaming.
myth.ithoth: The Book of Thoth, the forbidden book of all magic: a golden box inside a box of ivory and ebony, inside a box of silver, opened at last in a dark tomb.
myth.ithrl: A frost thrall: a gaunt spirit made of ice and frozen mist in the shape of a man, its body cracked and glittering, frost spreading from its feet across the stones.
myth.itut: A tutor of scribes: an elderly scribe teacher with a cane in a shaded schoolroom courtyard, boys copying texts on boards in front of him.
myth.iunwr: Unwriting: painted hieroglyphs lifting off an open papyrus scroll and dissolving back into drifting droplets of black and red ink in the air above it. Only the scroll and the dissolving signs, no person and no god.
myth.iwas: A was-sceptre: the long sceptre of power with its animal-head top and forked base, standing upright in a ray of light before an altar. The sceptre is the whole picture.
myth.iweret: Weret-Hekau, Great of Magic: a lioness-headed goddess with a sun disc and cobra on her head, rearing up with arms spread as magic crackles between her hands, protective serpent amulets coiling in the air around her.
myth.iwnd: A wind spirit: a translucent spirit made of swirling air and leaves, shaped like a dancing girl, spinning over a mountain.
myth.iword: The amulet of words: a small lapis-and-gold amulet shaped like a papyrus roll on a cord, glowing faintly, lying on an open scroll.
myth.jack: A desert jackal: a lean golden jackal trotting across the dunes at dusk, ears pricked, looking back over its shoulder.
myth.jarl: The fallen jarl: a dead Norse lord lying in state in a ship-grave, in his best armour with his sword on his chest and his shield at his feet, grave goods around him, a crowd of mourners as dim shapes.
myth.javel: A volley of javelins arcing through a dawn sky over a beach where black ships are drawn up.
myth.jbck: The deep takes back: a huge dark wave rising over a beach and pulling warriors and boats out to sea.
myth.jcrw: A brine-wyrm attacking a longship: a barnacle-crusted sea beast coiling around a small Viking longship, its long body looping over and under the hull, the crew tiny on the deck.
myth.jgrp: A drowning grip: the coils of a sea serpent wrapping around a longship and dragging it under the waves.
myth.jguard: A jackal guard: a black jackal lying watchful on top of a shrine chest, like the statue of Anubis in a tomb, eyes gleaming.
myth.jorm: Jormungandr, the World Serpent: the vast serpent that circles the world rising from the ocean, its head enormous against a stormy sky, venom dripping from its fangs, the sea boiling around it.
myth.jpack: A jackal packleader: a big black jackal leading a pack down a desert ridge at night, the others' eyes glowing behind it.
myth.jsnk: A sea-snake, child of the World Serpent: a huge green-scaled sea serpent rising out of grey waves, its head reared high, water streaming off it.
myth.jspt: Venom spray: a spray of glowing green venom bursting from beneath the sea's surface across a ship's deck.
myth.karma: The three Fates in a dark cave: one spinning the thread of life, one measuring it, one about to cut it with shears.
myth.kvas: The mead of Kvasir, brewed from the blood of the wisest of beings: three great vessels, the kettle Odrerir and the crocks Bodn and Son, brimming with glowing golden mead in a dark dwarf's cave.
myth.lamp: Lampetia, the shining nymph, daughter of Helios, herding her father's golden cattle across a sunlit meadow on Thrinacia.
myth.lava: A lava hound: a hound made of black volcanic rock with molten lava glowing through the cracks, flames dripping from its jaws, prowling over a lava field.
myth.lbow: A Lotus-Eater archer with a reed blowpipe and darts tipped with poppy, crouching among lotus flowers.
myth.lcurse: Loki's mischief: a warrior staring in horror as his sword turns into a snake in his hand.
myth.leon: Leonidas, King of Sparta, a bearded king in a red cloak and a crested bronze helmet, holding a large round bronze shield, standing calm and proud in a narrow mountain pass at sunset.
myth.lgale: A wind of mischief: a sudden whirlwind of leaves and snow sweeping a warrior off his feet, a laughing face in the swirl of wind.
myth.lhz: A shimmering golden haze hanging over the island of the Lotus-Eaters, lotus flowers floating in the air, the sea faint and dreamlike.
myth.libation: Odysseus pouring a dark offering into a trench in the ground at the edge of the world, as pale shades gather to drink.
myth.lion: A lioness of Sekhmet: a powerful lioness charging across the desert in the red light of sunset, sand flying from her paws.
myth.loki: Loki in hiding after Baldr's death, from the Prose Edda: the sly, red-haired trickster sits in his remote mountain house by the fire, knotting the very first fishing net from linen cord.
myth.lokib: Barbed words: Loki at a feast, leaning forward with a cruel smile and pointing, his insults shown as sharp glowing thorns flying from his mouth.
myth.lokis: Loki the shapeshifter: the red-haired trickster god grinning as he changes shape, his body breaking into a flock of birds, a salmon and a mare at the edges of his cloak.
myth.lot: A Lotus-Eater, a lean, smiling man crowned with lotus flowers, holding out the honey-sweet lotus fruit that makes travellers forget their way home.
myth.lrav: Loki's raven: a sly black raven with an unnaturally knowing grin, perched on a twisted branch, a stolen gold ring glinting in its beak, purple dusk behind it.
myth.lsnare: Loki's trick: a warrior frozen mid-step, tangled in near-invisible glowing threads, a sly shadow of Loki laughing behind him.
myth.lstd: The last stand of the doomed: three battered warriors back to back on a hilltop, shields up and weapons out, surrounded and outnumbered, fierce and unafraid.
myth.ltax: Loki's toll: a grinning Loki holding out his open palm for payment at a narrow bridge, a pile of gold rings at his feet.
myth.lure: The Sirens' meadow seen from the sea: flowers and a golden glow luring a ship toward hidden rocks.
myth.lurk: A Nile lurker: only the eyes and snout of a crocodile showing above the green water among papyrus reeds, ripples spreading.
myth.lyre: A golden lyre resting on a sea-worn rock, its strings glowing faintly, waves breaking below at twilight.
myth.mac6: The six-eared macaque, the false Great Sage: a dark-furred imposter of the Monkey King with six pointed ears, in black armour and a dark cap, his staff dark iron.
myth.mape: A mimic ape: a grey-furred ape with a long face, caught halfway through copying a heavenly soldier standing opposite it; one half of the ape already wears the soldier's gilded armour and plumed helmet.
myth.mead: The mead of poetry: a great carved drinking horn overflowing with golden mead that glows with light, held up in a dark hall.
myth.mear: A listening ear: a macaque crouched on a temple roof with six huge ears fanned out around its head, listening to the whole world, eyes closed.
myth.mecho: The echo of the staff: two iron staffs, one solid black iron and one a pale ghostly copy of it, crashing down side by side onto a stone floor at the same instant.
myth.medic: Machaon, son of Asclepius and surgeon of the Greek army at Troy, binding a wounded warrior's leg inside a lamp-lit tent.
myth.melody: Odysseus bound to the mast of his ship, straining against the ropes as the Sirens' enchanting melody washes over him, his crew rowing with wax in their ears.
myth.mgnt: A Muspel giant: a towering fire giant with skin of glowing rock and a beard of flame, raising a burning axe against a sky of smoke and fire.
myth.mhall: Mead-hall fury: a wide view down the length of a long, firelit mead hall in the middle of a wild brawl: benches overturned, drinking horns and mead flying through the air, a dozen warriors wrestling.
myth.mimr: Mimir's well: the severed, living head of the wise god Mimir resting at the edge of a dark pool beneath the roots of the world-tree, his eyes open and knowing, Odin's eye shining at the bottom of the water.
myth.mino: The Minotaur, the bull-headed son of the Cretan queen, in the dark stone corridors of the Labyrinth at Knossos, torchlight and bones on the floor.
myth.mjol: Mjolnir, the hammer of Thor: the short-handled iron hammer alone, resting on a snow-covered runestone, its head carved with interlaced beasts.
myth.mmon: A shadow monkey: a monkey made entirely of black shadow and smoke, only its glowing eyes clear, slipping along a temple wall.
myth.mourner: A mourning shade, a veiled ghostly woman holding a withered rose, weeping in the gloom of Erebus.
myth.mouth: The mouth of the Cyclops's cave sealed by an enormous boulder, firelight glowing through the gap, sheep pressed inside.
myth.mpill: A Cicone pillager carrying a flaming torch past a burning storehouse at night.
myth.mraid: A Cicone raider of Thrace with a battle axe and a round painted shield, charging out of the dawn mist.
myth.mskirm: A Cicone skirmisher with twin short swords, leaping over a low stone wall in the hills of Ismarus.
myth.mspear: A molten spear: a spear of glowing molten rock dripping fire as it flies through smoke.
myth.mthief: The master of thieves: a confident, scarred robber chief lounging on a pile of stolen treasure in a hidden cave, a gold collar on his neck, tossing a ring in his hand.
myth.mtrump: The second self: two identical figures standing back to back, one in light and one in shadow, joined by a thread of smoke, on an empty stage.
myth.mumw: A tomb mummy: a wrapped mummy shuffling out of a dark burial chamber, linen strips trailing, one arm reaching forward.
myth.muni: Muninn, Odin's raven of Memory: a black raven perched on an old moss-covered runestone, and drifting out of its dark feathers like smoke are faint, ghostly scenes of the past: a longship at sea, a burning hall, warriors long dead.
myth.muse: A Muse playing a lyre by a spring on Mount Helicon under the stars, a young poet listening, entranced.
myth.myrsh: A Myrmidon shield-bearer, one of Achilles' disciplined warriors from Phthia: a hard-faced hoplite in dark bronze armour and a black-crested helmet bracing a huge round shield painted with the ant emblem of the Myrmidons.
myth.nausi: Nausicaa, the Phaeacian princess, by the river mouth where she and her maids washed clothes, turning in surprise as a stranger appears.
myth.navig: A Phaeacian navigator at the stern of a ship that steers itself by thought alone, gazing at the stars above a calm sea.
myth.ndoom: A doom decree: a runestone carved with a sentence of fate glowing red, a crack splitting through it.
myth.neith: Phaethusa, the radiant nymph, daughter of Helios, with a shepherd's crook, glowing softly at dawn among the sacred herd.
myth.nidh: Nidhogg, the corpse-gnawer: the black dragon of the dead coiled among the dark roots beneath the world, gnawing a root with its huge fanged jaws, its scales dull as ash.
myth.nike: Nike, the winged goddess of victory, swooping down over a battlefield with a laurel wreath in her hand, her robes whipping in the wind.
myth.norn: The Norns, Urd, Verdandi and Skuld, who weave the fate of gods and men: three tall cloaked women, one old, one in her prime, one young and veiled.
myth.nshade: A dark, glinting draught of nightshade in a small clay vessel, purple nightshade berries and leaves around it, faint violet vapour.
myth.nspin: A thread-spinner: a hooded figure spinning a single glowing thread from a distaff, the thread running out of the picture.
myth.nwarr: A doomed warrior: a young warrior standing calm and resigned, a single golden thread of fate running from his chest and about to be cut by shears above him.
myth.oarsman: A Phaeacian oarsman pulling at the oar of a swift, sleek ship on a calm sea, the island of Scheria behind.
myth.oath: A blood oath: two warriors' hands clasped over a ring of iron, a thin line of blood running from a fresh cut across each palm into a bowl, a knife and a runestone beside it, firelight on the scene.
myth.odn: Odin the Allfather in all his power: a tall, gaunt old king with one blazing eye and a dark empty socket, long grey beard, a wide-brimmed hat and a dark blue cloak over mail.
myth.ofr: A pyre of heroes, seen from a distance: a tall, square funeral pyre of stacked logs blazing on a bare headland above a dark sea at night, a warrior's cloaked body lying on top of it, flames and sparks streaming up into the sky.
myth.ossuary: The inside of a beehive tomb like the Treasury of Atreus at Mycenae: bones, bronze helmets and grave gifts laid in the dark, a single shaft of light from the doorway.
myth.othala: Othala, the rune of heritage: the rune Othala carved deep into the door-post of an old ancestral longhouse, glowing softly, with the carved faces of ancestors around it.
myth.ouro: The ouroboros: the World Serpent biting its own tail, its body forming a vast ring around a small dark world in a black sea.
myth.owl: The little owl of Athena with wide golden eyes, gliding on silent wings over the moonlit Acropolis.
myth.ox: A white ox with gilded horns and a garland of flowers being led to the altar for sacrifice, as in the Homeric rites, smoke and a priest waiting.
myth.palm: The five-finger mountain: five immense peaks shaped like fingers standing in a ring in a sea of clouds, a golden talisman fluttering at the summit of the tallest.
myth.pdis: A stone disciple: a stone statue of a monk on a mountain path slowly coming to life, cracks of golden light in its body, eyes opening.
myth.pegasus: Pegasus, the winged white horse born from the blood of Medusa, rearing in flight above the clouds at dawn.
myth.peltast: A light-armed Greek skirmisher with a crescent-shaped wicker shield, running and hurling a javelin.
myth.pent: Penthesilea, queen of the Amazons, charging into battle at Troy on horseback with a double-headed axe and a crescent shield.
myth.pfin: A finger of the mountain: a single colossal stone pillar shaped like a finger rising from the clouds, carved with sutras.
myth.pgrd: A mountain warden: a stone guardian lion-dog on a temple step, its stone mane cracked and mossy, its eyes glowing gold.
myth.pgrow: The pack grows: a ring of glowing wolf eyes in the darkness of a snowy forest at night, more and more pairs appearing between the trees, one great black wolf at the centre.
myth.phguard: A guard of Scheria in polished bronze, standing before the gleaming golden gates of King Alcinous's palace.
myth.pikeman: A guard of the Taphians, the sea-raiding people of the Odyssey, with a long pike and a hide shield, standing watch over a rocky harbour.
myth.pit: A dark pit at the edge of the underworld, pale ghostly hands and faces rising from its depths in the mist.
myth.plague: A bringer of plague: a dark messenger of Sekhmet with a lion's mask and a quiver of glowing arrows, loosing them over a city at night.
myth.plm: The Buddha's palm: the serene Tathagata Buddha seen from far below, seated on a lotus among clouds, his right hand raised in the gesture of blessing, golden light pouring from his palm.
myth.plunder: Raiders carrying golden vessels and a bronze tripod out of a burning temple at night, the cult statue watching from the flames.
myth.poly: Polyphemus the Cyclops, son of Poseidon, the giant one-eyed shepherd standing at the mouth of his cave with a whole tree for a staff.
myth.priam: King Priam of Troy, a white-bearded old king in royal robes, looking out from the walls of his city.
myth.priest: A Poppy Priest of the Lotus-Eaters in a robe of red poppies, swinging a smoking censer, sweet drowsy smoke curling around him.
myth.pup: A wolf pup of Fenrir's brood: a small, fierce black wolf cub with oversized paws and glowing yellow eyes, snarling on a snowy rock, already showing its fangs.
myth.pyre: A towering funeral pyre burning on the beach at Troy at night, like the pyre of Patroclus, sparks spiralling up to the stars.
myth.pythia: The Pythia, the oracle of Delphi, seated on a bronze tripod in the dark inner temple, entranced, holding a laurel sprig as vapours rise around her.
myth.rage: Berserkergang, the battle-fury: a berserker's face in extreme close-up, teeth bared, veins standing out, eyes rolled and wild, foam at his mouth and a shield rim between his teeth.
myth.raidr: A young Ithacan raider leaping over the side of a black ship into the surf of a foreign beach, a short sword in one hand and a small round shield on his arm, salt-stiff hair flying, grinning with excitement.
myth.rally: A herald on a hilltop blowing a war horn as the scattered Greek warriors below rise and turn back toward the fight.
myth.ram: Warriors under a wooden roof swinging a bronze-headed battering ram against a great city gate, splinters flying.
myth.rampart: The towering walls of Troy, which the myths say Poseidon and Apollo built, seen from below at dusk, torches burning along the battlements.
myth.rboy: Red Boy, the Holy Infant King, son of the Bull Demon King: a fierce child demon with a red bib and a fire-tipped spear, breathing True Samadhi Fire from his mouth and nose, standing on five carts of fire.
myth.reaper: A tall plant creature of woven lotus stems and drooping poppy heads, holding a crescent sickle, standing in a misty field of sleep.
myth.reaver: A hooded assassin in shadow dipping arrowheads into poison from a small clay pot, like the arrow-poison Odysseus sought at Ephyra.
myth.regin: Regin the smith: a cunning, scheming dwarf smith with a crooked smile, reforging the broken sword Gram at his anvil.
myth.reir: The rune of Eir: a small wooden rune-stave carved with a healing rune, tied with red thread and hanging from a warrior's belt, glowing softly.
myth.rend: The skull-splitter: a great bearded axe buried in a split iron helmet on a battlefield, snow and blood around it. The axe and helmet are the whole picture.
myth.requiem: Mourners lamenting over a fallen warrior laid on a bier, arms raised in grief as on ancient Greek funeral vases, torches against a dark sky.
myth.rflm: A fire-cloud blast: a rolling blast of red and gold fire bursting across a ravine, curling like the clouds in a painting.
myth.rfly: The raven banner: a white triangular war banner with a black raven on it, streaming in a strong wind on a tall pole, its raven seeming to flap its wings.
myth.rgrd: A Samadhi guard: a demon guard in red armour whose spear and helmet plume are made of living fire, standing before a burning cave mouth.
myth.rimew: A rime-witch, a giantess of the frost: a tall, gaunt jotun woman with blue-white skin and hair like icicles, raising a hand that freezes the air into a spiral of ice.
myth.rimp: A fire-wheel imp: a small grinning red demon riding a spinning wheel of flame, spitting sparks.
myth.roar: Roar of the wolf-coats: a pack of wolf-pelted warriors roaring together in a line, faces up, weapons raised, the shock of their roar bending the snow and mist around them.
myth.rser: A rune-carver at work: an old bearded man in a fur hood kneeling before a tall grey runestone, carving a serpent band of runes with chisel and mallet, painting the cut lines red by the light of a small fire.
myth.rspr: A fire-cloud spearman: a demon soldier riding a small cloud of fire, throwing a burning spear.
myth.ruru: Uruz, the rune of strength: the rune Uruz carved deep into a standing stone, glowing, with the great horns of a wild aurochs rising behind it in the mist.
myth.rwall: The rimewall: a towering wall of blue glacier ice blocking a mountain pass, with huge frost giants dimly visible inside the ice like shadows.
myth.sack: Odysseus's men sacking and burning Ismarus, city of the Cicones, at night, the first raid on the voyage home from Troy.
myth.sacril: The angry sun god Helios glaring down from his blazing chariot onto the island of Thrinacia, the sacred herd below.
myth.sailor: A sailor of Odysseus's fleet straining at the oar of a black-hulled Greek ship with painted eyes on its prow, spray flying, the wine-dark sea at dusk.
myth.sails: The white sails of a Phaeacian ship filled with a favouring wind, racing over a bright sea.
myth.salve: Asclepius, the god of healing, with his staff entwined by a single serpent, gently applying a salve to a wounded warrior's arm.
myth.sand: A sandstorm: a towering wall of red-brown sand rolling across the desert toward a caravan, swallowing the sky.
myth.sapper: A Trojan saboteur creeping through the night with a torch and a pick, undermining the wooden palisade of the Greek camp.
myth.sbrood: A scorpion brood: a swarm of small black scorpions pouring out from under a cracked stone slab in the desert, tails raised.
myth.scav: A battlefield scavenger: a hunched figure in a hooded cloak picking through the shields and swords of the fallen on a misty battlefield at dawn, a raven on a broken spear beside him.
myth.scorch: A blinding ray of sunlight scorching down from the sky onto a rocky shore, the air shimmering with heat.
myth.scout: A small Siren as the Greeks painted her, a woman's head on a bird's body, perched on a sea rock, watching for passing ships.
myth.scrb: A rune-scribe: a young woman carefully cutting runes into a wooden stick with a small knife by candlelight, a row of finished rune-staves before her.
myth.scyl: Scylla, the six-headed monster of the strait, her six heads on long necks rising from her cave high in a sea cliff above a passing ship.
myth.seid: A seidr hex: a sorceress's hands weaving a curse in the air, threads of dark light spinning from her fingers around a carved staff.
myth.sekh: The eye of Ra: a huge blazing eye of fire in the sky, a lioness's shape inside the flames, scorching the desert below.
myth.sekhg: Sekhmet, the eye of Ra: the lioness-headed goddess of war in a red dress with a sun disc and cobra on her head, roaring with flames streaming from her mouth across the desert.
myth.sent: An Argive sentinel on night watch on the earthen wall the Greeks built to guard their ships at Troy, a tall shield planted beside him, watch-fires behind.
myth.serk: Serket's venom: the goddess Serket with a scorpion on her head, holding up a glowing cup of venom, scorpions circling her feet.
myth.setb: The beast of Set: a lean dog-like animal with a curved snout, tall square-topped ears and a forked tail, prowling the red desert.
myth.setg: Set, lord of the red desert: the god with the head of a strange curved-snouted beast and tall square ears, in red and gold, holding a was-sceptre in a howling desert storm.
myth.setst: A storm of the desert: a black thundercloud of sand and lightning sweeping over the red desert, a beast-shaped head faintly visible in the storm.
myth.setx: The dismemberment: the coffin of Osiris floating down the Nile at night, Set's shadow looming over it on the riverbank.
myth.sfire: True Samadhi fire: a fire that water cannot quench, pouring down a mountainside in red, gold and blue flames, rain hissing into steam above it.
myth.sh1: One of Scylla's six heads on a long snake-like neck snapping out from a sea cave, rows of teeth bared.
myth.sh2: A gnashing head of Scylla on a long neck, emerging from the mist of her cliff cave, teeth bared.
myth.sh3: A head of Scylla that bays like a hound, its long neck stretched out from the cave, mouth open in a howl.
myth.sh4: A green, venomous head of Scylla on a long sinuous neck, dripping venom, lunging from the dark cave.
myth.shab: The shabti oath: hundreds of small shabti figures standing in ranks in a tomb, all raising their hoes together as if answering a call.
myth.shade1: A restless shade of the dead, a pale translucent figure drifting in grey mist at the edge of the underworld.
myth.shbs: A shabti servant: a small blue faience shabti figurine with a hoe and basket coming to life in a tomb, stepping off its shelf among rows of others.
myth.sheep: A fat, woolly ram from the flock of Polyphemus standing in the Cyclops's cave, the kind Odysseus clung beneath to escape.
myth.shield: The Shield of Achilles that the smith god Hephaestus forged, its bronze face worked in rings showing earth, sea, sky, cities at peace and at war, glowing on the anvil of his forge.
myth.shmd: A Norse shield-maiden in the front rank of a shield wall on a pebble beach as longships land behind her: a young woman with a fierce, set face, braided hair under a plain iron helmet.
myth.shoal: Jagged rocks just beneath the surface of a dark sea, foam breaking over them, a ship's broken oar caught among them.
myth.sigur: Sigurd the Dragon-Slayer from the Volsunga saga, just after slaying the dragon Fafnir: the young hero kneels by a fire, the reforged sword Gram across his knees.
myth.sip: A hand offering a clay cup of honeyed lotus drink, sweet golden vapour rising from it, on a sunlit island shore.
myth.siren: A Siren of Anthemoessa, the flowery island of the Sirens: a bird-woman with great wings spread, singing among flowers above the sea, Odysseus's ship far below.
myth.skal: A skaldic bard: a young poet standing on a bench in a crowded hall, reciting with one arm raised, a gold arm-ring flashing.
myth.skar: Skar the Scarred, a veteran berserker: a grizzled warrior with a face crossed by old scars and one milky eye, braided beard, bare scarred arms and a notched sword, grinning grimly.
myth.skies: A chorus of Sirens circling in a stormy twilight sky above the sea, wings wide, singing together.
myth.sking: The scorpion king: a fierce early king of Egypt in the white crown with a scorpion emblem on his standard, raising a ceremonial mace before his army.
myth.skinw: A skin-changer: a figure halfway through turning from a man into a fox, their body twisting, half of the face a sly fox's muzzle.
myth.skld: A skald of the fallen: a grey-haired poet sitting by a fire with a lyre, singing of the dead, the faces of slain warriors faint in the smoke above him.
myth.skoll: Skoll, the wolf who chases the sun: an enormous red-gold wolf racing across a dawn sky after a low, pale sun, its fur streaming like fire.
myth.skul: The Skull-Cleaver, a Norse champion: a broad warrior in mail with a huge bearded axe raised in both hands, mid-swing, wood splinters and snow flying.
myth.skuld: Skuld, maiden of the future: a young woman with her face hidden by a veil, holding a pair of shears and a scroll of runes, half valkyrie, a spear at her side.
myth.slei: Sleipnir, Odin's eight-legged grey horse, the finest of all steeds: a powerful, storm-grey stallion with eight legs, wild mane and steaming breath, galloping through the air above the clouds, runes carved on its bridle; empty.
myth.slst: A slain-strike: a ghostly spear thrown by a dead warrior's spirit, glowing pale as it flies over a battlefield.
myth.snake: A temple cobra: a rearing cobra with its hood spread, coiled on a temple altar beside offerings of bread and fruit.
myth.sobek: Sobek, lord of the waters: the crocodile-headed god in a gold collar and kilt, a sun disc and plumes on his head, rising from the Nile with a was-sceptre.
myth.sobk: The jaws of Sobek: the enormous open jaws of a crocodile seen from inside, framing a boat on the river beyond.
myth.sobpr: A priest of Sobek: a priest feeding a sacred crocodile adorned with gold earrings and bracelets in a temple pool.
myth.song: A Siren with a woman's face and a bird's wings and body, singing from a rock in the sea, her song rippling visibly through the air.
myth.soulw: A wailing soul: a pale, translucent dead spirit with its hands to its face, wailing in the grey mist of the underworld.
myth.spd1: A cave spiderling: a small, glossy black spider-spirit the size of a cat with a tiny human face, scuttling out of a crack in a cave wall, silk trailing behind it.
myth.spd2: A silk-spinner: a spider spirit in the form of a pale young woman in white silk, threads of glistening silk pouring from her navel and spreading across a cave mouth like curtains.
myth.spd3: A web-weaver: a large spider with jade-green markings hanging in the centre of an enormous web strung between two stone pillars, dewdrops glittering on the silk.
myth.spdq: The spider-spirit matron: the queen of the seven spider spirits of Silk Cave, a tall beautiful woman in layered silk robes whose shadow on the cave wall is a giant spider, smaller spiderlings clinging to her sleeves.
myth.spear: A seasoned Ithacan spearman, a grown soldier in a simple bronze helmet and linen cuirass, braced behind a round bronze shield, spear levelled, on the rocky shore of Ithaca with a dark sea behind him at dusk.
myth.spearc: A bronze-tipped spear hurled across the plain of Troy in a duel before the city walls, caught mid-flight, dust and a blood-red setting sun behind it.
myth.sphg: A sphinx guardian: one of a long avenue of ram-headed sphinx statues lining the approach to a temple, the nearest one turning its head.
myth.sphinx: The Sphinx of Thebes, with a woman's face, a lion's body and an eagle's wings, perched on a rock outside the city to pose her riddle, bones scattered below.
myth.sphinx2: The Great Sphinx: the colossal lion-bodied sphinx with a pharaoh's head lying before the pyramids at Giza, its eyes slowly opening as if waking.
myth.sphs: A desert sentinel: a winged sphinx standing guard on a rocky outcrop above the desert, wings half spread, watching the horizon.
myth.sphx: The riddle of the sphinx: a traveller standing small before a great sphinx at night under the stars, the sphinx leaning down to speak.
myth.spoils: A heap of plunder on a beach beside a black ship: bronze tripods, golden cups, captured armour and shields, glinting in torchlight.
myth.sprm: A spear-marked thrall: a young bondsman with a red mark of a spear painted on his chest, kneeling with his head bowed as an offering to Odin before battle, rope around his wrists.
myth.squeen: Serket's handmaiden: a priestess of the scorpion goddess with a scorpion crown, live scorpions crawling harmlessly over her arms as she raises a bowl of venom.
myth.sstalk: A sand stalker: a huge pale desert scorpion half buried in the sand, only its pincers and raised stinger showing as it waits.
myth.star: Starkad, the ageless hero of the sagas, cursed by Thor and granted three lifetimes by Odin: a huge, grim old warrior with a long grey beard, a scarred, weathered face and hard eyes, a bearskin over battered mail.
myth.stdb: A standard-bearer: a young warrior holding high a tall pole with a raven banner streaming in the wind, shouting the warband forward.
myth.sting: The sting of Serket: a giant scorpion's tail curling down and striking, venom glistening at its tip. The sting is the whole picture.
myth.sunch: The chariot of the sun: Helios's golden chariot racing across the sky, drawn by four fiery horses with manes of flame, sparks streaming from its wheels.
myth.surtr: Surtr, lord of Muspelheim: the black fire giant with a flaming sword brighter than the sun, his face dark and terrible, a crown of flames, standing amid a sea of fire.
myth.tblk: A shield dummy: a wooden training figure like a wing-chun wooden man, holding a large round rattan shield in front of itself, standing in a bamboo grove practice ground.
myth.tbrute: A straw brute: a big, heavy straw dummy built like a wrestler, stuffed into an old bronze breastplate with a wooden club strapped to its arm.
myth.tbull: The great white bull that Poseidon sent from the sea to King Minos, rising out of the waves onto the shore of Crete.
myth.tdig: A tunnel digger: a sweating robber chipping through the stone of a tomb wall with a copper chisel, rubble around his knees, a rope leading back up a narrow shaft.
myth.tdum: A training dummy in a sandy Greek practice yard by the sea: a figure of straw and sacking lashed to a wooden post, wearing a dented old bronze helmet and a battered round shield, spear-holes in its chest.
myth.telem: Telemachus, the grown son of Odysseus, standing at the prow of a ship leaving Ithaca to seek news of his father, the goddess Athena beside him disguised as old Mentor.
myth.testudo: Warriors crouched under a locked roof of shields as a rain of arrows and stones falls on them from a city wall.
myth.tgiant: The clay giant: a huge figure of a soldier sculpted from Nile mud, twice the height of a man, standing guard with a clay shield, cracks drying in the sun and priests' handprints still in the clay.
myth.tguard: The mummy king: a mummified pharaoh in a crumbling gold-trimmed shroud and the double crown, standing in his burial chamber with a crook and flail, his painted eyes glowing.
myth.thanat: Thanatos, the winged god of death, a solemn dark-winged young man holding an upside-down extinguished torch, gliding silently over a battlefield at dusk.
myth.thegn: A thegn of the hall, kneeling: a young retainer in a fine red embroidered tunic kneeling on one knee before his lord's high seat and offering his sword up hilt-first with both hands, his head bowed.
myth.thermo: The narrow pass of Thermopylae between cliffs and the sea, a small line of Greek shields facing an endless Persian host at sunset.
myth.thess: A Thessalian horseman galloping across the plains of Thessaly, cloak streaming, javelin raised, a storm sky over the mountains behind.
myth.thor: Thor in full fury: the thunder god in mid-swing, hurling Mjolnir with one arm, lightning exploding from the hammer and wrapping around his whole body, his eyes blazing white with lightning.
myth.thrl: A thrall, a Norse bondsman: a thin, ragged young man with a shaved head and an iron collar, in a coarse undyed wool tunic, gripping a wood-axe as he is pushed into battle, fear and stubborn hope in his face.
myth.thunder: Zeus hurling a jagged thunderbolt from the storm clouds, striking Odysseus's ship at sea as punishment for eating the sacred cattle of Helios.
myth.tide: A gentle, glowing tide washing over a wounded warrior lying on a sunlit beach, healing light in the water.
myth.titan: A colossal stone giant asleep on the island of the Lotus-Eaters, overgrown with lotus vines, one heavy eye half open.
myth.tithe: The tithe of the slain: two valkyries in mail riding low over a battlefield at dusk, each lifting the glowing spirit of a fallen warrior from among the dead, taking their share for Valhalla and Folkvangr.
myth.tiwa: Tiwaz, the rune of victory: the arrow-shaped rune Tiwaz cut into a spearhead, glowing hot, the spear held up against the sky.
myth.tmedj: A Medjay of the temple: a tall, lean desert warrior in a white kilt and red sash with an ostrich-feather in his hair, a bow over his shoulder and a long spear, guarding a temple doorway.
myth.torch: Torchlight: a burning reed torch thrust into a dark tomb corridor, its light falling on painted walls and startling a nest of bats.
