myth.tpen: A reed pen: a scribe's reed pen dipped in black ink, the ink trail it leaves on papyrus lifting off the page and turning into a flying bird.
myth.trident: The trident of Poseidon rising from a stormy sea, crackling with power, waves rearing around it.
myth.trob: Grave-goods: a robbed tomb chamber heaped with gilded chairs, chests, chariots and statues, a robbers' rope hanging down through a hole in the ceiling.
myth.tscar: A scarab amulet: a single large carved scarab of lapis lazuli and gold with outspread falcon wings, resting on folded white linen, glowing faintly. The amulet is the whole picture.
myth.tscr: A temple scribe: a young scribe sitting cross-legged in the classic pose with a papyrus roll across his kilt, a reed pen behind his ear, ink palette at his side, in a sunlit courtyard.
myth.tspear: A straw spearman: a straw dummy holding a long wooden spear, lashed onto a sled that warriors are shoving through the snow toward the viewer.
myth.tsun: Sunder the soul: a priest raising an ostrich-feather fan over a dying warrior as his soul parts in two, the Ka rising as a pale double of his body with raised arms on its head, the Ba flying free as a human-headed bird.
myth.tyr: Tyr the one-handed, god of war and oaths: a stern, broad-shouldered god with one hand missing at the wrist, holding his sword in the other, the shadow of the wolf Fenrir who bit off his hand looming faintly behind him.
myth.ulf: A young Ulfhednar initiate pulling a grey wolf pelt over his head and shoulders for the first time, the wolf skull resting on his brow, in a forest clearing at night lit by one fire.
myth.ulfk: Ulf, the Berserk King: a towering king of the wolf-warriors, wearing a great black wolf pelt like a mantle and an iron circlet, his bare chest painted with runes, a huge two-handed axe resting on his shoulder.
myth.undertow: A powerful undertow dragging a ship's anchor and rope down into the dark, swirling water.
myth.unwor: The unworthy dead: a line of ghostly souls whose hearts were heavier than the feather, cast into a lake of fire in the underworld.
myth.urd: Urd, keeper of the past: an ancient woman in grey robes with white hair, holding a spindle of old faded threads, sitting at the edge of a glowing well.
myth.valk: A valkyrie, a chooser of the slain, riding a dark horse low over a misty battlefield at dusk: a stern young woman in mail and a plain iron helmet with a spear, her cloak streaming.
myth.verd: Verdandi, weaver of the present: a woman in her prime at a great loom, weaving a shining tapestry of fate, her hands quick and sure.
myth.veteran: A grey-bearded Athenian hoplite with old scars, standing on the marshy plain of Marathon, the burial mound of the fallen behind him.
myth.vfea: The feast of heroes: a great roasting boar on a spit over a long fire in Valhalla, horns of mead raised by warriors' hands around it.
myth.vinit: A Valhalla initiate: a young warrior, freshly slain, standing uncertainly at the golden doors of Valhalla in his torn and bloodied tunic, a valkyrie's hand on his shoulder guiding him in.
myth.vlnd: Volund the smith: the legendary master smith at his forge, hammering a glowing sword on the anvil, sparks flying, his face grim and determined.
myth.vmar: Marshalling the dead: a warlord raising his sword in a cold fog, the faint spirits of his fallen warriors rising behind him to stand in ranks.
myth.volv: The volva, a Norse seeress: a woman in a dark blue cloak and a black lambskin hood lined with white cat fur, seated on a high platform, holding her iron staff topped with a brass knob.
myth.wacro: An acrobat monkey: a monkey in a red vest balancing upside down on one hand at the very top of a tall bamboo pole, juggling peaches with its feet.
myth.wall: A wall of round aspis shields painted with bold emblems (a scorpion, a Gorgon's face, a charging bull), locked together, seen close up.
myth.walls: The great walls of Troy rising over the plain at sunset, the Scaean Gates shut tight.
myth.warden: A warden of the dead in dark bronze armour, standing guard before the gates of Erebus with a long spear.
myth.waugury: A peach-pit augury: an old monkey fortune-teller casting peach pits onto a bronze tray marked with the eight trigrams, reading the pattern by lantern light.
myth.wbear: A staff-bearer: a broad, muscular monkey warrior carrying an enormous iron staff across his shoulders with both arms hooked over it, grinning with effort.
myth.wbigstaff: The staff of ten thousand jin, the thirteen-and-a-half-thousand-pound iron pillar of the Dragon King's sea palace: the vast golden-banded staff crashing down from the clouds onto a mountain.
myth.wblock: A whirling staff: a long iron staff spinning in front of a monkey defender like a shield, arrows bouncing off the blurred golden circle.
myth.wbreak: The heaven-breaker: the great golden gate of a heavenly palace bursting inward in a storm of splintered timber, gilded studs and dust.
myth.wburn: Burning the ledger: the Ledger of Life and Death lying open on a black lacquer lectern in the hall of the underworld, its pages with names crossed out in thick black ink.
myth.wchamel: A chameleon monkey: a monkey whose fur is changing colour and pattern to blend into a temple wall painting, only its grinning eyes giving it away.
myth.wchange: The seventy-two changes: a swirling scroll of transformations, a monkey shape melting from a tiger into a bird into a fish into a temple, each form flowing into the next.
myth.wclone: Clones of the Great Sage: Sun Wukong blowing on a handful of plucked golden hairs that turn mid-air into a crowd of identical little monkey warriors with staffs, each tumbling and grinning.
myth.wcloudh: A hair whirl: a spinning ring of glowing golden hairs rising into the night sky like a halo above a mountain temple, each hair turning into a tiny curling cloud. No figures.
myth.wcloudm: A cloud rider: a young monkey warrior crouched on a small curling cloud as if surfing, racing through the sky past misty mountain peaks, its tail streaming behind.
myth.wcloudr: A somersault strike: a monkey warrior flipping over an enemy's shield wall on a puff of cloud, staff swinging down from above.
myth.wcounter: A counter-strike: a heavenly soldier in gilded armour flipping head over heels through the air, his halberd twisted out of his hands by a staff that enters from the edge of the picture.
myth.wcycle: Full circle: the Taoist yin-yang symbol drawn as a great swirling ring of cloud and ink in the sky, with the eight trigrams around it.
myth.wdance: Dancing away: a laughing monkey spinning out of reach of a lumbering demon's grasping hands, silk ribbons trailing.
myth.wdart: A hair dart: a single golden hair plucked by the Monkey King turning into a glowing dart in mid-flight, a sharp streak of light against the sky.
myth.wdisc: A disciple of the Sage: a young monkey student in a plain grey robe practising staff forms alone on a mountain ledge at dawn, intent and focused.
myth.wdodge: A quick dodge: a nimble monkey bending backward as a sword slices through the air just above its nose, its tail curling for balance.
myth.wdrink: The stolen elixir: Laozi's golden gourds of the elixir of immortality tipped over on a table, golden pills spilling out and glowing.
myth.wdrum: A drum-beater monkey: a monkey pounding a big red war drum with two sticks, its face fierce and joyful, its fur flying with the rhythm.
myth.wecho: An afterimage: a trail of five fading white-ink ghost outlines of a small grey-furred monkey in a plain tunic, arcing across a moonlit temple courtyard in a single leap, each outline more transparent than the last.
myth.wepw: Wepwawet, the opener of ways: the wolf-headed god in white and gold standing on a standard at the front of an army, a mace and a bow in his hands, the desert road opening ahead.
myth.wfan: The mountain-felling gale: Princess Iron Fan, in red and gold silk robes, swinging her giant palm-leaf fan with both hands.
myth.wfeint: A feint: a demon swinging its axe at a monkey that turns out to be only a puff of smoke and a falling hair, the real monkey's shadow behind it.
myth.wflurry: A flurry of blows: a big horned demon reeling backward, surrounded by dozens of swirling streaks of brush ink and golden blurs striking from every side, too fast to see the attacker.
myth.wfoot: Nimble footwork: a monkey's quick feet dancing across a row of floating stepping stones over a rushing river, each step leaving a ripple.
myth.wfurn: The Eight-Trigram Furnace of Laozi: the great bronze cauldron-furnace engraved with the eight trigrams, blazing with fire, the lid bursting open as the Monkey King leaps out unharmed, his eyes now burning gold from the smoke.
myth.wgate: A guard of the Jade Gate of Heaven: a towering heavenly guardian in ornate green-and-gold armour with a fierce painted face, holding a halberd before huge jade gates in the clouds.
myth.wgreat: A great wall monkey: a giant stone monkey statue standing guard on a watchtower of a long mountain wall, moss on its shoulders, a staff in its fist.
myth.wgrow: Grow tall: a small monkey soldier growing to giant size in a single moment, towering over a mountain pass, tiny enemy soldiers staring up at him in shock.
myth.wgust: An iron fan gust: a giant palm-leaf fan sweeping across the picture and blowing a demon soldier head over heels into the distance.
myth.whair: A spare hair: a single golden hair from the Monkey King drifting on the wind like a tiny comet, glowing, sparks and a faint curl of cloud trailing from it against misty peaks.
myth.wheist: The heavenly heist: a furry brown hand reaching through a silk curtain into Laozi's alchemy chamber to snatch a gourd of golden elixir pills from a lacquered shelf. Only the hand and the shelf.
myth.whirl: The whirlpool Charybdis seen from above, a vast spiral of dark sea, a ship's timbers caught at its rim.
myth.whstorm: A hair storm: a whirlwind of glowing golden hairs tearing across a battlefield like a sandstorm, demon soldiers shielding their faces. No monkey in the picture.
myth.wight: A barrow-wight: a gaunt, skeletal dead king in a crown and rotted robes, sitting on a throne inside his burial mound among his grave goods, cold light in his eyes.
myth.wjug: A juggler monkey: a plain brown macaque with no armour, no cape and no cap, wearing only a simple undyed cotton tunic with a red ribbon in its fur, standing on a big drum at a village festival and juggling peaches.
myth.wking: Sun Wukong, the Great Sage Equal to Heaven, in his full glory: the Monkey King with golden fur and blazing fiery golden eyes, wearing a phoenix-feather cap with two long pheasant plumes, golden chain mail.
myth.wledger: Erased from the ledger: a judge of the underworld in black robes staring in dismay at a brush stroke that has wiped a name from the Ledger of Life and Death, the ink still wet.
myth.wlegion: A hair-born legion: rank upon rank of identical little monkey soldiers in plain grey tunics marching out of the mist in perfect lines with spears and banners, seen from the side. No leader figure, no gold armour.
myth.wmillion: A million monkeys: a whole mountain valley filled to the horizon with monkey warriors, banners and spears, seen from high above like an ocean of golden fur.
myth.wmirm: A mirror monkey: a monkey peering into a round bronze mirror whose reflection grins back and steps out of the glass as a second monkey.
myth.wmirror: A mirror hair: a single golden hair floating between two facing bronze mirrors, its reflections multiplying into an endless tunnel of glowing hairs.
myth.wmist: A mist veil: a thick, glowing mist rolling over a mountain battlefield, the shapes of soldiers lost and confused inside it, a monkey's sly face faintly visible in the swirl.
myth.wmonk: A mountain monkey of Flower-Fruit Mountain: a small, bright-eyed golden monkey leaping from rock to rock beside a waterfall, a fruit in its hand.
myth.wmount: The Five Elements Mountain: the Buddha's giant open palm turning into five stone peaks that press down on the tiny Monkey King trapped beneath.
myth.wmyriad: Myriad staffs: a sky full of hundreds of golden-banded iron staffs raining down like spears onto a heavenly army camp.
myth.wnez: Nezha, the lotus-born champion: a fierce boy warrior with two hair buns, standing on his flaming Wind Fire Wheels, the red silk Armillary Sash flowing around him, a golden ring on one arm and the Fire-Tipped Spear in his hand.
myth.wnull: The nothingness monk: an old, serene monk sitting cross-legged in meditation, his body fading into empty air and drifting ink, only his calm face and folded hands still clear.
myth.wolf: A great grey wolf of the iron wood, running flat out through deep snow, its whole lean body stretched in mid-leap, snow spraying from its paws, pine trunks streaking past.
myth.worchard: An orchard raid: a troop of monkeys raiding the Heavenly Peach Garden at night, climbing the trees and tossing peaches down into baskets while a sleeping guard snores below.
myth.wpeachc: The peaches of immortality: three huge glowing peaches, pink and gold, hanging from a gnarled branch of the immortal tree, each with a faint halo. The peaches are the whole picture.
myth.wpeachg: The Queen Mother of the West's Peach Banquet: a long golden banquet table in a jade palace among the clouds, laden with huge immortal peaches, wine jars and dishes, lanterns glowing, the guests not yet arrived.
myth.wpeachk: A peach keeper of the Heavenly Peach Garden: a small, mischievous monkey sitting on a gnarled branch of the immortal peach tree, cradling a huge glowing peach and taking a big bite, peach blossoms falling around it.
myth.wpierce: The fire-eyed gaze: two blazing golden eyes with fiery pupils glaring out of darkness, twin beams of golden light shooting from them and burning through a demon's disguise. Only the eyes, nothing else of the face.
myth.wpig: Zhu Bajie, the Pig of the Eight Prohibitions, once Marshal of the Heavenly Canopy: a huge pot-bellied pig-faced warrior with big floppy ears and a greedy, cheerful grin, in a loose black monk's robe.
myth.wpluck: Pluck a hair: a golden monkey hand plucking a single glowing hair, the hair already starting to shimmer and change. Only the hand and the hair.
myth.wpocket: Shrink to a needle: Sun Wukong shrinking his huge staff down to the size of an embroidery needle and tucking it behind his ear, the staff glowing as it shrinks.
myth.wqt: Equal to Heaven: the Jade Emperor's great dragon throne in the Hall of Divine Mists standing empty, a monkey's half-eaten peach left on its silk cushion, the golden-banded iron staff leaning against its arm.
myth.wrally: Rally the troops: hundreds of plain brown monkey soldiers with spears and red banners cheering below the great waterfall of the Water Curtain Cave, seen from behind the crowd. No single hero figure.
myth.wrod: The iron rod: the golden-banded iron staff spinning end over end through the air like a thrown spear, trailing a ribbon of golden light across a clear blue sky. The staff is the whole picture.
myth.wrout: Rout of the heavenly host: a whole army of heavenly soldiers in gilded armour fleeing in panic across the clouds, banners snapped, helmets and halberds tumbling through the sky.
myth.wruyi: The Ruyi Jingu Bang, the golden-banded iron staff that was once the pillar measuring the depth of the Eastern Sea: the staff alone, growing enormous as it stands upright out of the waves like a pillar into the clouds.
myth.wsandy: Sha Wujing, the sand monk, once a heavenly general banished to the Flowing Sands River: a tall, grim, blue-skinned monk with a red beard and a necklace of nine skulls, carrying his crescent-moon spade.
myth.wseal: The five-finger seal: the Buddha's enormous palm closing from the sky, its five fingers turning into stone pillars, a golden light pouring from the centre.
myth.wsent: A monkey sentry: a young monkey warrior in a red headband on watch at the top of a rocky crag, shading its eyes with one hand, a short spear in the other, banners of Flower-Fruit Mountain fluttering.
myth.wsix: The six-eared macaque, the Monkey King's perfect double: an ape identical to Sun Wukong in cap, armour and staff, but with six ears and a cold, sly look, half of its body still shimmering mid-change.
myth.wskin: Shed a skin: an empty, perfect monkey-shaped husk of golden fur standing on a rock, the real monkey already gone in a swirl of mist.
myth.wslip: Slip away: a monkey squeezing out through a gap in a heavenly prison's golden bars, a jailer asleep on his stool outside.
myth.wsmash: A staff smash: the end of a golden-banded iron staff slamming into a stone courtyard, the flagstones shattering outward in a ring, stones and ink-splash flying.
myth.wsomer: A cloud somersault: Sun Wukong curled into a tight somersault on a cloud, streaking across the sky in a long golden arc that covers thousands of miles.
myth.wspin: A staff spin: a monkey warrior of Flower-Fruit Mountain spinning a long staff so fast it becomes a blurred golden wheel, leaves and dust whirling around it in a bamboo grove.
myth.wsplit: A heaven-splitting blow: the sky itself cleaved in two by a single blinding crack of golden light running down through the clouds, the jade palaces of heaven tilting apart on either side. No figures, only the split sky.
myth.wstep: A cloud step: a single foot stepping onto a small curling cloud that appears beneath it in mid-air over a drop.
myth.wtang: Tang Sanzang, the gentle monk on the pilgrimage to fetch the scriptures: a serene young monk with a shaved head, wearing the embroidered red-and-gold kasaya robe and the five-Buddha crown.
myth.wthou: A thousand hairs: Sun Wukong, seen from behind on a mountain top, blowing a great cloud of golden hairs from his palm into the wind, the hairs spreading out over the valley like a golden storm.
myth.wtree: The immortal peach tree of the Queen Mother of the West, which fruits once in three thousand years: a vast, ancient peach tree in full blossom on a mountain in the clouds, its branches heavy with glowing fruit.
myth.wtroop: A hair-born troop: a squad of six small identical grey-furred monkeys in plain undyed tunics, bare-headed, springing up out of a scatter of glowing golden hairs on a stone courtyard.
myth.wtypes: Three forms: a hanging scroll with three painted panels of the same a plain brown macaque with no armour, no cape and no cap, wearing only a simple undyed cotton tunic: one with a staff, one leaping on a cloud.
myth.wulf: A wolf-coat warrior charging: an ulfhednar with a grey wolf pelt over his head and back, bared teeth, a spear in each hand, running low through a snowy birch forest.
myth.wunravel: Unravel existence: a demon dissolving into loose threads of ink that unwind and drift away into the mist, its outline coming apart.
myth.wunward: Reveal the true form: a bronze demon-revealing mirror held up, its light falling on a beautiful lady whose shadow on the wall is a skeleton demon.
myth.wvang: The whirlwind vanguard: a plain brown macaque with no armour, no cape and no cap, wearing only a simple undyed cotton tunic racing ahead of a column of monkey soldiers inside a spinning whirlwind of dust and leaves.
myth.wvolley: A hair volley: hundreds of golden hairs turning into glowing darts mid-flight, streaking across a sky toward a line of demon soldiers who raise their shields. No monkey in the picture, only the volley and its targets.
myth.wwind: A windborne monkey: a plain brown macaque with no armour, no cape and no cap, wearing only a simple undyed cotton tunic riding a gust of wind high over misty peaks, arms spread like wings, its simple tunic flapping.
myth.wwine: Heavenly wine: a jade wine cup and a tipped-over porcelain jar of heavenly wine on a cloud, the glowing wine spilling into the sky like a stream of light.
myth.wxform: Transformation: a small monkey in a swirl of smoke turning into a fierce armoured demon general, half of it still monkey and half already demon.
myth.yall: The All-Seeing Scribe: Thoth himself, the ibis-headed god in a white kilt and broad collar, seated cross-legged with a reed pen and a scribe's palette, writing on a papyrus that stretches up into the sky.
myth.ybab: A baboon of the dawn: a sacred baboon sitting on a temple pylon with its arms raised to greet the rising sun, a crescent moon and disc on its head, the sun's first rays striking its fur.
myth.ybat: A wind-riding bat: a giant demon bat with tattered yellow wings riding a gust of sandy wind over a ridge.
myth.yclerk: A temple archivist: a scribe in a vast archive room climbing a ladder to reach a jar of rolled papyri on a high shelf, lamp in hand.
myth.ycopy: A scribe's copy: seen from directly above, two identical papyrus scrolls lying side by side on a reed mat with ink cakes, brushes and a water pot, only a scribe's two hands visible as one copies the last line.
myth.ycount: Countermeasure: two war chariots meeting head-on in the desert, one charioteer raising a shield that catches every arrow aimed at him.
myth.ydef: A ridge guard: a hunched demon sentry in sand-coloured armour on a rocky ridge, shielding its eyes from blowing sand.
myth.yechoes: Echoes of the past: ghostly faded copies of an ancient army marching across the desert through the heat haze, their outlines flickering.
myth.yfore: Foreknowledge: an oracle priestess in a dark shrine gazing into a bowl of oil and water, a vision of the future glowing on its surface.
myth.ygale: The three-sacrifice gale: a towering column of yellow wind tearing across a valley, uprooting trees and blinding soldiers.
myth.ygen: The Yellow Wind Monster, a yellow marten demon: a lean, sharp-faced demon king with golden fur and a trident, blowing a howling yellow storm of sand from his mouth.
myth.ygg: Yggdrasil, the world-ash: one immense, ancient ash tree, unmistakably a tree, standing alone on a rise above a sea of mist.
myth.yhall: The hall of records: a vast hypostyle hall of painted columns, every column covered in records, lit by shafts of light from the high windows.
myth.yibis: An ibis of Thoth: a sacred white ibis with black head and long curved beak wading in the shallows of the Nile among papyrus reeds, one foot raised, the reflection of a crescent moon in the water.
myth.yjudge: A judge of words: a stern judge in a long robe with the feather of Ma'at pinned to his collar, pointing a finger at an accused man in a courtroom of columns.
myth.ykhon: Khonsu, the moon-traveller: a young god with the sidelock of youth and a crescent moon cradling a full moon disc on his head, wrapped like a mummy and holding a crook and flail, travelling across the night sky in a silver boat.
myth.yledger: A ledger of deeds: a wide view of a royal granary courtyard at harvest, workers carrying sacks and pouring grain into heaps while a scribe sits small in the shade recording the count, cattle and carts beyond.
myth.ypre: Preempt: a hand closing a temple door just as an enemy's spear-point thrusts through the gap, catching it.
myth.yprep: Lay the snare: hunters in a papyrus marsh stretching a clap-net between the reeds, waiting for a flock of ducks to land.
myth.yread: Read the signs: a priest watching a flock of birds wheel across the sunset sky over the Nile, reading their pattern as an omen.
myth.yrecall: Recorded history: a long wall relief of a famous battle with chariots and archers, its painted figures faintly coming alive and stepping off the wall.
myth.ysage: A sage of Hermopolis: an old, wise priest of the city of Thoth sitting beneath a palm tree with a sacred ibis beside him, teaching from a scroll.
myth.ysenet: Senet with the Moon: Thoth playing the board game senet against Khonsu, the moon god, on a moonlit temple roof, winning five extra days of light from the moon; the glowing moon disc above, the board between them.
myth.ystar: A star-reader: a priest-astronomer on a temple roof at night holding a merkhet sighting tool up to the stars, the sky full of the constellations of Egyptian astronomy.
myth.ytig: A tiger vanguard: a tiger demon standing upright in armour, with a striped face and a broadsword, roaring at the front of a demon army.
myth.ytrap: Ambush foretold: archers hidden among desert rocks with bows drawn, waiting as an enemy chariot approaches below, unaware.
myth.ytruth: Ma'at's ledger: the goddess Ma'at, a woman with a tall ostrich feather on her headband and outspread winged arms, kneeling over an open book of truth that glows gold.
myth.yvizier: The vizier's report: the vizier, a dignified official in a long white robe and a gold collar, kneeling before the throne to read a report from a scroll.
myth.ywarn: Forewarned: a sentry on a desert fort's wall shading his eyes and pointing at dust rising on the horizon, a horn at his lips.
myth.ywatch: A watcher at the gate: a stern gatekeeper demon of the underworld with a knife in each hand and the head of a ram, sitting before a closed door in the Duat.
myth.ywind: The yellow wind: a whole landscape swallowed by a churning yellow sandstorm, a pagoda and pines just visible through it.
myth.zerk: A frenzied warrior possessed by Ares, eyes wild, mouth open in a war cry, charging, while the war god's red shadow looms behind him in the smoke.
myth.zeus: A white marble altar of Zeus on a mountain-top at night, offering smoke rising from it, a crackling bolt of lightning striking down onto the altar from a storm-black sky.
